newsitem.title: USA: AMP to cut about 1,000 jobs in restructuring.
newsitem.headline: AMP to cut about 1,000 jobs in restructuring.

text.p: AMP Inc., a leading supplier of electrical connectors, said Wednesday it will reorganize some businesses, resulting in the loss of about 1,000 jobs worldwide.
The move follows AMP's announcement on Dec. 31 that it would restructure its businesses and take a $195 million charge in the fourth quarter.
Officials at the Harrisburg, Pa.-based company, whose products include plugs, sockets and wiring systems, were not immediately available to comment.
Under the restructuring, AMP will discontinue under-performing product lines and realign manufacturing operations, primarily in its Americas operations.

The company said it aimed to reduce its presence in the market for military cylindrical pin and socket connectors, which will result in the closing of a California plant and a cutting of some Pennsylvania jobs.
AMP also said its CIR-PAC unit will exit some areas of the printed wiring board business, resulting in the closing of its Riverhead, N.Y.-based unit over the next two quarters.
The company will close or consolidate its specialised facilities in Roanoke, Va., and McSherrystown, Pa., it said, and also eliminate certain Connectware products in its Global Interconnect unit.

AMP has nearly 45,000 employees in Asia, Europe and the Americas, serving customers in the communications, networking, industrial, consumer goods, aerospace and automotive industries. AMP had sales of $5.2 billion in 1995.
AMP's stock fell 62.5 cents to $39 on the New York Stock Exchange.
